deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the working behind Riemann's 1860 paper 'Über die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite'. The page treats the isothermal (Boyle–Mariotte) case, with pressure P = a^2 ρ and constant sound speed a.

(0) Diagram. The x–t plane is drawn with a ray from the origin, labelled 0. This is the trajectory x = ξ(t) of a discontinuity. The two later sketches show a wave profile with a vertical jump: a steepened wave that has become a shock.

(1) Set-up. The unknowns are ρ(x,t) and u(x,t). Just behind the jump (x = ξ−0) the state is (ρ1, u1); just ahead (x = ξ+0) it is (ρ2, u2). The velocities relative to the moving jump are v1 = u1 − ξ'(t) and v2 = u2 − ξ'(t).

(2) Mass balance. Through a cross-section ω during time dt: v1 ρ1 ω dt = v2 ρ2 ω dt, so ρ1 v1 = ρ2 v2.

(3) Momentum balance. The momentum change of the mass flux equals the pressure difference: (v2 − v1) ρ1 v1 ω dt = a^2 (ρ1 − ρ2) ω dt. Equivalently ρ1 v1^2 + a^2 ρ1 = ρ2 v2^2 + a^2 ρ2.

(4) Solving. Substitute v2 = v1 ρ1/ρ2 (my step) to get (ρ1/ρ2 − 1) v1^2 ρ1 = a^2 (ρ1 − ρ2). Hence:
- v1^2 = a^2 ρ2/ρ1 and v2^2 = a^2 ρ1/ρ2;
- v1 = ±a√(ρ2/ρ1) and v2 = ±a√(ρ1/ρ2), with the same sign since ρ1 v1 = ρ2 v2.

(5) Shock speed. Using ξ' = u_i − v_i, there are two families:
- ξ' = u1 + a√(ρ2/ρ1) = u2 + a√(ρ1/ρ2), the forward-facing shock;
- ξ' = u1 − a√(ρ2/ρ1) = u2 − a√(ρ1/ρ2), the backward-facing shock.

(6) Riemann invariants. Take p = log ρ + u/a and q = log ρ − u/a. From ρ_t + (ρu)_x = 0 and u_t + u u_x + a^2 (log ρ)_x = 0 one gets:
- ∂p/∂t = −(u+a) ∂p/∂x;
- ∂q/∂t = −(u−a) ∂q/∂x.
So p is carried with speed u+a (noted in the margin) and q with speed u−a.

(7) Admissibility. For the forward shock with ρ1 > ρ2: u1 + a > ξ' > u2 + a. Indeed u1 + a√(ρ2/ρ1) < u1 + a and u2 + a√(ρ1/ρ2) > u2 + a. So the p-characteristics on both sides run into the shock: the compressive (Lax-type) shock condition.

(8) Jump relations. Write Δ for (state 1) − (state 2). Equating the two forms of ξ' gives u1 − u2 = a(√(ρ1/ρ2) − √(ρ2/ρ1)), i.e.
Δu/a = e^{Δlogρ/2} − e^{−Δlogρ/2} = 2 sinh(Δlogρ/2).
With Δp = Δlogρ + Δu/a, Riemann then wants Δu/a in terms of the invariant jumps.

The next page continues: with α = √(ρ1/ρ2), Δp = 2 log α + α − 1/α. Correspondingly Δq = 2 log α − (α − 1/α), which is O((Δlogρ)^3). This is the classical fact that the jump of the 'other' invariant across a weak shock is third order.
errors: The last equation reads Δu/a = Δlogρ − Δp. From Δp = Δlogρ + Δu/a one has Δu/a = Δp − Δlogρ. The written form is correct only if Δp is replaced by Δq, since Δq = Δlogρ − Δu/a gives Δu/a = Δlogρ − Δq. So this is either a sign slip or a p/q slip.
In '(ρ1/ρ2 − 1) v1^2 ρ1 = aa ρ1 − ρ2' the parentheses around (ρ1 − ρ2) are omitted; this is notational only.
Not on this page: the next page's copy writes u2 − a√(ρ2/ρ1) where u2 − a√(ρ1/ρ2) is meant; it is correct here.
Unjustified step: the momentum balance is used without any energy equation. This is consistent only because the isothermal law P = a^2 ρ is assumed, so the page is not wrong in its own setting.

results.what: Mass and momentum jump conditions across a moving discontinuity for an isothermal gas: ρ1 v1 = ρ2 v2 and ρ1 v1^2 + a^2 ρ1 = ρ2 v2^2 + a^2 ρ2, giving v1^2 = a^2 ρ2/ρ1 and v2^2 = a^2 ρ1/ρ2.
results.usually_credited_to: Stokes 1848 and Riemann 1860 (mass/momentum), Rankine 1870, Hugoniot 1887–89 (with energy)

results.what: Shock speed ξ' = u1 ± a√(ρ2/ρ1) = u2 ± a√(ρ1/ρ2).
results.modern_name: Shock speed for the isothermal p-system

results.what: Characteristic form with p = log ρ + u/a and q = log ρ − u/a transported at speeds u ± a.
For a forward compression shock (ρ1 > ρ2): u1 + a > ξ' > u2 + a.
results.usually_credited_to: Lax 1957 in general form; Riemann 1860 discussed admissibility of compression shocks

results.what: Velocity jump across a shock: Δu/a = 2 sinh(½ Δ log ρ), i.e. (u1−u2)/a = (ρ1−ρ2)/√(ρ1ρ2).
results.modern_name: Hugoniot curve of the isothermal Euler / p-system in (log ρ, u) coordinates

deep.surprise_reason: This is draft material for Riemann's published 1860 Luftwellen paper: shock jump conditions, Riemann invariants and the compressive shock condition, all known as his. The only mildly interesting details are the explicit Lax-type inequality and the sinh form of the Hugoniot curve, both essentially in the paper.

transcription_corrections: The line '[-u_1-] ∂ξ/∂t = v1' should read 'u1 − ∂ξ/∂t = v1'. The u1 is overwritten or blotted, not deleted, matching u2 − ∂ξ/∂t = v2.
In the line 'x = ξ − 0' the first x appears overwritten. The pair x = ξ−0 / x = ξ+0 denotes the two sides of the discontinuity.
The third balance line shows a struck-out factor. The intended equation is (v2 − v1) ρ1 v1 ω ∂t = aa(ρ1 − ρ2) ω ∂t.
The 'u+a' written beside p = log ρ + u/a is a marginal note giving the propagation speed of p, not part of the formula.
